note.question: How does the retail industry depends extensively on store liquidation, both to allow managers of going concerns to divest stores in efforts to enhance performance and as a means for investors to recover capital from failed ventures?
note.overview: Store liquidation is the time-constrained divestment of retail outlets through an in-store sale of inventory. The retail industry depends extensively on store liquidation, both to allow managers of going concerns to divest stores in efforts to enhance performance and as a means for investors to recover capital from failed ventures. Retailers sell billions of dollars of inventory annually during store liquidations.
